results.rule: lineup better only if the pooled 95% interval of ridge WRMSE minus lineup WRMSE lies above zero and the lineup model is lower in more than half of the test seasons; ridge better by the mirror rule; otherwise no difference

selection.rule: lowest possession-weighted stint margin RMSE pooled over the selection seasons; ties: larger ridge penalty; smaller model, then larger interaction penalty

coverage.excluded_games: R01's admission (IM02 + event gate) excluded 3 to 26 games a season; their stints are not in the sealed bundles. Counts and reasons: docs/evidence/research/r01/coverage.json.
leakage_plan: Rolling origin: a fit for target season t reads stints and boxes from seasons t-3..t-1 only, so every input is dated before t's opener.
Selection seasons 2021-22 and 2022-23, test seasons 2023-24 to 2025-26, fixed here.
Cold-start status and box features for a target season come from the window only; a player first seen in t reads the newcomer value.

verdict.rule: R08's: pooled 95% interval of the RMSE gain excludes zero, and the same metric has the lower RMSE in more than half of the common seasons; otherwise no ranking

caveats: Stint margins are very noisy: every model, ridge included, misses a stint's margin by 92 to 96 points per 100 possessions on the test seasons. Differences between models are fractions of a point.
The verdict is the registered rule's, on three held-out seasons. A gain whose interval includes zero is not a difference.
Each fit is made at the start of a season from the three seasons before it and is not updated during the season.
Players with fewer than 1,000 possessions in the window, and newcomers, read a box-score fallback that knows nothing about draft position or college.
The lineup tool predicts a five against a fixed panel of 2025-26's most-used lineups at a neutral site. It is a model output, not a forecast of how that five will play.

The similarity map is one fit's player vectors squeezed into two dimensions by UMAP. Its axes, directions and the distances between groups mean nothing; it is not a style or position map. In this fit the seeds agree on nearest neighbours no more often than chance, so the map shows no stable structure.
The selected lineup model's interaction is almost zero (its predictions correlate with ridge's above 0.99999999), so the lineup tool's two numbers are nearly identical.
The per-model error table was restored from the saved test weights after a defect in the frozen runner overwrote it; the restored numbers reproduce every frozen gain exactly.
